sentences.text: The anterior sacral vertebrae feature articular processes oriented horizontally, with pre-epipophyses extending forward beyond the articular facets. A distinct crest runs between these processes and splits into two branches.

In the middle tail region, the posterior articular processes project far behind the front edge of the vertebral bodies. The neural spines here slope backward or lie flat, while the bone itself is notably massive.
A unique feature identified in 2021 is a high, triangular plate-like crest on the front tail vertebrae that projects downward, separating the rear hump from the rest of the body.
Tengrisaurus was formally described in 2017 by Averianov and Skutschas based on three caudal vertebrae collected from the Murtoi Formation.

The fossil record began with Georgi Dmitriev reporting a procoelous sauropod vertebra near Murtoy in 1960. Alexei Starkov found another vertebra and osteoderms in 1992, followed by Pavel Skutschas locating a third in 1998. A fourth vertebra was excavated at the same site in 1999 with the help of G. I. Sazonov.

The genus name means 'Tengri lizard' and honors Tengri, the main god of the Mongols, while the species name honors Starkov. This dinosaur holds the distinction of being the first named from Transbaikalia and the first sauropod named from Russia.
In 2025, Averianov and colleagues included a newly described cervical vertebra in their phylogenetic analysis of the genus.
It inhabited the Murtoi Formation of Russia during the Early Cretaceous.
